takeaway: Hot, sunny and gusty this weekend and Monday, around 34°C in Nicoya, with offshore winds every morning and a solid southwest swell (6–9 ft at 15–16 seconds) peaking Sunday. Next week is the story: the early-November rain spell looks wetter again and now runs Tuesday Nov 3 through Friday Nov 6, with Wednesday and Thursday the heaviest days. The trades fade from Tuesday and Pacific onshore winds take over by Wednesday night. No tropical storm threat, but the prolonged-rain watch edges up to moderate.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sat Oct 31 – Mon Nov 2)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds and occasional gusts on the North Pacific all day today, with gusts of 30–60 km/h and stronger in the mountains and northern Guanacaste. Nicoya's high is about 34°C with a low near 22°C. IMN's weekly outlook says afternoon showers become possible over the Nicoya Peninsula from this weekend, but the central and western North Pacific keeps a low rain chance. The models keep Nosara at about 2 mm a day Saturday and Sunday and about 4–6 mm Monday. Showers this weekend favor the Caribbean side and southern Costa Rica.
periods.implications: Great outdoor days, especially mornings. It's hot and windy, so bring water and expect dust. A stray afternoon shower is possible but most hours stay dry.
periods.confidence: High on hot, breezy and mostly dry. Moderate on whether a stray afternoon shower reaches Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Tue Nov 3 – Fri Nov 6)
periods.pattern: The trade winds fade from Tuesday and the shower belt that has been sitting south of Costa Rica moves north over Nicoya. IMN expects a weak tropical wave to cross early in the week. Every model average puts about 22 mm (just under an inch) at Nosara on Tuesday. The European and American averages then jump to about 48 mm (nearly 2 inches) on Wednesday, with about 29–48 mm Thursday and about 22 mm Friday. The European AI average and the regular runs are lighter, about 11–29 mm a day. This is Pacific-side rain fed by southwest winds, not Caribbean rain.
periods.implications: Get outdoor plans done by Monday. Keep Tuesday through Friday flexible: expect afternoon and evening downpours with thunder, and a real chance of a longer soaking on Wednesday or Thursday. Watch for muddy roads, fast-rising creeks and river crossings.
periods.confidence: High on Nov 3–5 turning wet. Moderate on how heavy, since the averages are wetter than the single runs. Low on exact amounts.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Sat Nov 7 – Sat Nov 14)
periods.pattern: Rain tapers off over the weekend of Nov 7–8 as the trade winds return over Nicaragua. The model averages drop to about 6 mm around Nov 8 and about 1–4 mm a day for Nov 10–14. One American run keeps some showers around Nov 12–14, but the averages don't. IMN's long-range outlook (issued Oct 26) still calls for drier than normal weather through Nov 22, with the dry season settling in on the North Pacific in early November and very dry conditions returning Nov 9–15.
periods.implications: Expect a dry-out through the second week of November. Plans from about Nov 9 onward look like the safest bet.
periods.confidence: Moderate on drying out after Nov 7. Low on timing and on any late stray showers.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, so it's offshore at Nosara every morning through Monday, strongest tonight. The trades weaken Tuesday, go light and southeasterly Tuesday night and Wednesday, and turn onshore from the southwest and west by Wednesday night.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 1:35 a.m. Pacific time, 2:35 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast winds of 15–20 knots today with 6–8 ft of southwest swell at 15 seconds. Tonight the Gulf of Papagayo gusts up to 20–25 knots. Sunday is northeast to east 15–20 knots with 6–9 ft at 16 seconds, the swell peak. Monday is northeast 15–20 with 5–7 ft, easing to east 10–15 Monday night and Tuesday with 4–6 ft at 14 seconds. Tuesday night and Wednesday turn southeast around 10 knots, then southwest to west 10–15 knots Wednesday night with 5–7 ft at 12–13 seconds, which is onshore at Nosara. The waters just south of the peninsula already go light or west around 10 knots this afternoon, and southwest 10–20 knots from Monday night to Wednesday, so Nosara afternoons can go side-on or onshore sooner than spots farther north. The marine forecast also flags scattered offshore showers and storms tonight through Sunday night. Nicaragua looks offshore all day through Monday, a good sign for clean Nosara mornings, but that doesn't mean Nosara holds offshore all day.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Sunday and Monday at first light for the biggest, longest-period swell with offshore wind; it will be windy, so go early before it gets bumpy and hard to paddle into. This morning is good too. Long-period sets come bigger and less often than the average height suggests, and rip currents run stronger. Tuesday morning is a likely last clean session; from Wednesday expect onshore, choppy conditions and rain.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings through Monday. Moderate on how long afternoons hold. Moderate to high on onshore winds by Wednesday night.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, edging up from low-to-moderate to moderate. No slow-spinning low is forecast, but the Nov 3–6 rain spell looks wetter and longer again.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Tuesday Nov 3 through Friday Nov 6, heaviest Wednesday and Thursday.
gyreWatch.supporting: The European and American averages now show about 48 mm at Nosara on Wednesday (up from about 29 mm yesterday) and keep rain going through Friday. The marine forecast brings southwest to west winds into the Gulf of Papagayo by Wednesday night and southwest winds of 15–20 knots just south of the peninsula on Wednesday, the kind of moist Pacific feed that drives temporales. The regular European run shows a broad band of west to southwest winds south of Costa Rica Wednesday and Thursday. IMN expects a weak tropical wave early next week, and NOAA's tropics outlook (Oct 27) says weaker easterly winds south of Mexico in the Nov 4–17 window could briefly favor a late-season East Pacific storm.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model average shows a closed low parked off Costa Rica, and the strongest southwest winds stay mostly offshore and to the south. The single model runs are noticeably lighter than the averages. The trades return over Nicaragua around Nov 7–10, cutting the spell short. IMN's long-range outlook still expects drier than normal weather through Nov 22. The U.S. hurricane center expects nothing near Central America; its only East Pacific area is far southeast of Hawaii (now 40% in 7 days), and nothing is expected in the Caribbean.

whatChanged: The early-November rain spell got wetter and a day longer again: the European and American averages now peak near 48 mm on Wednesday Nov 4 (yesterday's European peak was about 29–35 mm), and rain lingers into Friday Nov 6. The marine forecast now shows the switch to onshore southwest and west winds by Wednesday night. Sunday's trades eased a touch (now northeast to east 15–20 knots instead of 20–25), and the swell nudged up to 6–9 ft at 16 seconds on Sunday. The marine forecast adds scattered offshore showers and storms tonight through Sunday night. IMN's daily forecast keeps the North Pacific dry and gusty today. The hurricane center's area far southeast of Hawaii rose to 40%. No new IMN notices since Oct 25.
practical: Surf at first light Sunday and Monday for the biggest swell in offshore wind, and watch for strong rip currents. Do your outdoor plans and errands by Monday. Keep Tuesday through Friday (Nov 3–6) flexible for afternoon and evening downpours, with Wednesday and Thursday most likely to bring a longer soaking; be careful on dirt roads and at river crossings. Expect it to dry out from about Nov 8–9. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
